headline: CISA forced emergency patching of actively exploited SharePoint, Fortinet, and Oracle flaws as ransomware halted Coca-Cola's Fairlife and Japan's Nichirei food production.

emerging_trends.text: Ransomware crews keep knocking factory lines offline, stopping Coca-Cola's Fairlife milk plants and Japan's Nichirei frozen-food operations within days of each other, proof that production floors now rank among extortion's richest targets.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Ransomware Halts Fairlife and Nichirei Food Production

emerging_trends.text: Prompt injection has become the cross-site scripting of autonomous browsing, as the Claude for Chrome extension flaw and a new Agent Data Injection attack show how planted text steers an agent's clicks toward attacker goals.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Prompt Injection Becomes the Web Agent Era's XSS

emerging_trends.text: Attackers weaponize freshly disclosed flaws within days, and the SharePoint deserialization bug CVE-2026-58644 drew exploitation almost immediately after Microsoft shipped its fix.
emerging_trends.topic_title: SharePoint, Fortinet, and Oracle Flaws Under Active Attack

topics.title: SharePoint, Fortinet, and Oracle Flaws Under Active Attack
topics.latest_developments: CISA on July 16, 2026 added three actively exploited flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog—SharePoint deserialization bug CVE-2026-58644 rated 9.8, plus Fortinet FortiSandbox command-injection flaws CVE-2026-25089 and CVE-2026-39808—ordering agencies to patch SharePoint by July 19 and Fortinet by Sunday, while separately demanding a fix for an exploited Oracle E-Business Suite flaw by Saturday.
topics.summary: The SharePoint flaw lets remote, authenticated attackers run arbitrary code on the server, and attackers began exploiting it soon after disclosure; organizations running on-premises SharePoint, FortiSandbox, or Oracle E-Business Suite should patch immediately.

Fresh SharePoint Vulnerability Exploited Soon After Disclosure
CISA urges immediate action on actively exploited Fortinet flaws
CISA orders feds to patch actively exploited Oracle flaw by Saturday

topics.title: Ransomware Halts Fairlife and Nichirei Food Production
topics.latest_developments: The Coca-Cola Company detailed in a July 16, 2026 SEC Form 8-K that a ransomware attack suspended all US production at its Fairlife dairy subsidiary, and Japanese frozen-food giant Nichirei disclosed it disconnected its systems on July 13 after a cyberattack and began a gradual restoration.
topics.summary: Two food manufacturers halted production floors within days of one another; Coca-Cola says Fairlife product quality and safety stayed intact, and Nichirei is restoring operations while both companies assess the full scope.

topics.title: Prompt Injection Becomes the Web Agent Era's XSS
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer detailed a flaw in Anthropic's Claude for Chrome extension that lets a malicious extension simulate clicks to trigger predefined AI actions against Gmail, Google Docs, Calendar, and Salesforce, as UC Berkeley researchers named Cross-Site Prompting and built the Prismata defense, and researchers disclosed a new Agent Data Injection attack that corrupts the facts an agent trusts to make it misclick or run attacker commands.
topics.summary: Autonomous web agents read whatever a page displays and can treat stranger-supplied text as instructions; the emerging fixes range from Berkeley's Prismata filter to least-privilege identity binding, while text-salting phishing already slips past AI email filters in more than a million messages.

topics.title: Scattered Spider Pair Jailed for TfL Hack
topics.latest_developments: Woolwich Crown Court on July 16, 2026 sentenced Thalha Jubair, 20, of East London, and Owen Flowers, 18, of Walsall, to five and a half years each for the 2024 Transport for London breach that knocked out 148 systems and forced all 27,000 TfL employees into offices to reset their passwords in person.
topics.summary: The two members of the Scattered Spider collective pleaded guilty last month; the National Crime Agency put TfL's losses and recovery costs at roughly £29 million.

topics.title: ClickLock and OkoBot Stealers Hit macOS and Crypto
topics.latest_developments: A new macOS infostealer dubbed ClickLock arrives as a command pasted into Terminal, then kills Finder, the Dock, Spotlight, and Terminal on a loop roughly every 210 milliseconds until victims surrender their login password, hitting at least 100 users, while a separate framework called OkoBot deploys more than 20 payloads to steal cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases and credentials.
topics.summary: Both operations lean on social engineering and modular payloads to drain passwords and crypto; ClickLock installs two LaunchAgents for persistence, and users should refuse to paste unfamiliar Terminal commands or enter passwords into unexpected system dialogs.

sources.title: New ClickLock macOS malware traps users into revealing login password

topics.title: China-Linked Daxin Rootkit Resurfaces in Taiwan
topics.latest_developments: The Daxin kernel-mode rootkit that Symantec first documented in March 2022 resurfaced after more than four years inside a Taiwan manufacturing firm, alongside a previously unreported pre-login SYSTEM backdoor dubbed Stupig, while Kaspersky detailed GoSerpent backdoor attacks using Stowaway RAT and ThumbcacheService to steal data from Southeast Asian government entities.
topics.summary: Both campaigns point to persistent China-linked espionage against Asian manufacturing and government targets; defenders should hunt for the srt64.sys driver and the new Stupig implant that loads before login.

sources.title: Daxin Resurfaces in Taiwan Alongside Stupig Pre-Login SYSTEM Backdoor

business_politics.title: AI Trade Reverses, Chip Stocks Sell Off Worldwide
business_politics.latest_developments: The AI trade went into reverse Friday, July 17: U.S. semiconductor stocks headed for their worst week since 2025's 'liberation day' rout, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 fell nearly 5%, and Nasdaq futures dropped as investors questioned the pace of the AI buildout.
business_politics.summary: A global selloff hit chipmakers and AI-linked shares after IBM's preliminary results triggered a 25% stock plunge, its steepest ever, feeding fear that the spending underpinning the AI boom will not pay off; the rout dragged Asian and European markets and premarket U.S. futures lower.

business_politics.latest_developments: American forces widened their target list Friday, July 17, striking bridges and collapsing a tower at a key Iranian port, and crude headed for a weekly gain topping 10% as the U.S.-Iran fight escalated.
business_politics.summary: The United States has intensified its air campaign against Iran over the Strait of Hormuz, hitting infrastructure deeper inside the country; oil's double-digit weekly climb and strained refining capacity threaten to keep U.S. gasoline prices elevated for months even after crude eases.

business.latest_developments: Governor Josh Shapiro visited Gateway High School in Monroeville Thursday, July 16, to celebrate $678 million in new public-education money in the freshly signed state budget, part of $3 billion in increases—a 35% rise—over his administration.
business.summary: Pennsylvania's $50.8 billion budget, signed July 12, steers $678 million in new funding to public schools; officials at the Gateway School District credited earlier state increases with higher graduation rates and test scores.

around_town.title: Wildfire Smoke Pushes State to Code Purple, Relief Saturday
around_town.latest_developments: Wildfire smoke drove all of Pennsylvania to a Code Purple 'very unhealthy' alert Friday, July 17, with Allegheny County touching the hazardous 'maroon' range Thursday evening; forecasters expect Saturday storms to wash the smoke out.
around_town.summary: Smoke from wildfires in Canada and Minnesota blanketed Western Pennsylvania, sending fine-particulate pollution to hazardous levels; doctors reported patients with burning throats and eyes, and the Allegheny County Health Department urged residents to limit time outdoors.
